full_judgment: 10. With regard to the Criminal Appeal No. 731 of 1990 Mr. Khan firstly contended that there has been a serious embellishment in the prosecution case at different stages and the learned Additional Sessions Judge having not considered this aspect of the case committed error of law in convicting the appellants. He has further contended that the learned court below failed to weigh and sift the evidence in proper perspective and, as such, the impugned order of conviction is liable to be set aside. Mr. Khan lastly argued that there are material discrepancies in ocular evidence and moreover the prosecution withheld the material witnesses. The learned Additional Sessions Judge failed to notice this aspect of the case, as such, an adverse presumption ought to have been drawn against the prosecution case.
